user.title: Set up AirProce
user.description: AirProce connects directly to Home Assistant through the purifier's USR Socket B. MQTT is not required. Keep Socket A connected to the official AirProce cloud if you want to continue using the official app.

data.watchdog_silence: Seconds without a valid state before querying
data.watchdog_timeout: Seconds to wait for each watchdog query

data_description.usr_host: Use the purifier/USR module's LAN IP address. A DHCP reservation or static address is recommended.
data_description.listen_port: Configure the purifier's Socket B TCP client to connect to the Home Assistant LAN IP on this port. Each purifier needs a different listening port.
data_description.device_id: Optional. Leave blank to generate an ID from the USR IP. Once created, keep this value unchanged so entity IDs remain stable.
data_description.usr_username: Default USR modules commonly use admin.
data_description.usr_password: Default USR modules commonly use admin.
data_description.verify_usr_web: Checks reachability and HTTP Basic/Digest credentials. The integration does not change USR settings automatically.
data_description.listen_host: Normally keep 0.0.0.0. In the USR page, Socket B must point to the Home Assistant LAN IP, not 0.0.0.0.
data_description.watchdog_silence: The purifier normally reports about every 15 seconds. The default 45 seconds avoids unnecessary polling.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure AirProce
reconfigure.description: Update purifier, listener, USR login, or watchdog settings. The integration reloads automatically after saving.
